manifest.title: An internal business app
manifest.description: Only people with the company's email domain can sign in; roles decide what each can do; leavers lose access at once; every privileged action is logged.

appName.label: The app's name
appName.why: Used on the screens and as the project name

appPurpose.label: What does the app do? (who does what, and how)
appPurpose.why: It decides the data shape and how many screens there are
appPurpose.placeholder: e.g. Staff book equipment such as meeting-room projectors, and the office team records when it goes out and comes back

domain.label: Your company's email domain (e.g. example.co.jp)
domain.why: Only people with this domain will be able to sign in

workspace.label: Does your company use Google Workspace?
workspace.why: If it does, people can sign in with their company account as it is

external.label: Will people outside the company (clients, contractors and so on) use it too?
external.why: If so, it is no longer an internal app, so you will be pointed to another blueprint

externalWho.label: Which outside people, and what will they do?
externalWho.why: Used to choose the other blueprint
externalWho.placeholder: e.g. A supplier's contact checks how their orders from us are progressing

users.label: About how many people will use it?
users.why: A guide for the cost estimate and the budget alert

roles.label: The kinds of role (choose all that apply)
roles.why: It becomes the rules for who can do what

dataSensitivity.label: The most confidential information it handles
dataSensitivity.why: It decides how strict the audit log, the retention period and the storage place are

options.公開してよい情報のみ: Only information that may be public
options.社内限りの情報: Information for inside the company only
options.人事・給与・顧客の機密情報: Confidential HR, payroll or customer information

region.label: Where the data is stored
region.why: It cannot be changed once created

offboarding.label: When someone leaves or changes jobs, must they lose access the same day?
offboarding.why: If so, a way to force out even people who are signed in is added

existingProject.label: Do you already have a Firebase / Google Cloud project?
existingProject.why: Whether to create a new one or use the one you have

billingAccount.label: Do you have a Google Cloud billing account (a company card or similar)?

budget.label: The monthly budget limit (yen)
budget.why: You are notified when spending gets close to this amount

mainScreens.label: The main screens (as far as you know)
mainScreens.why: Decides which screens are built first
mainScreens.placeholder: e.g. the equipment list, a booking form, the office team's loan log

domain-restriction.title: Limit it to the company's domain
domain-restriction.description: Blocking functions refuse other domains at sign-in; the rules check the domain again.

roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.description: Roles live in custom claims, granted only by an admin-only function.

offboarding.title: Shut out people who leave or change jobs
offboarding.description: Revoke refresh tokens, drop claims, and make the rules refuse tokens issued before the revocation.

audit-log.title: Audit log
audit-log.description: Privileged actions are logged by functions into a collection clients cannot write.

verify-dev.title: Is the domain limit working on development?
verify-dev.description: The blocking functions are registered on the dev project, not only deployed.

production-auth.title: Turn on the production sign-in limit first
production-auth.description: Deploy functions and rules to production and register the blocking functions before the site itself is published.

ringi.title: Ringi (requests and approvals)
ringi.description: Staff write up a ringi (a request for approval), and approvers approve it or send it back in turn. Only people with the company's domain can sign in, and the audit log records who approved what and when. An internal example that runs on Firebase.
